public_rationale: Agentless reports measured inference costs for defined software tasks alongside their success rates. Errors and differing execution systems therefore do not make all task-cost measurement impossible. This contradicts the categorical claim under the ordinary reading of a reproducible measurement method. The finding is narrower than proving that complete business ROI is easy to measure. Other research supports Zitron's concern about inconsistent evaluation practices.
limitations: The result depends on reading standard measurement as a reproducible method rather than universal industry adoption.
Benchmark inference costs exclude some costs of deploying and supervising AI in a business.
The proposed causal mechanisms were not separately isolated.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Nobody can measure the ROI of AI or standardize the cost of a task, because LLMs inherently hallucinate and harnesses and interfaces keep multiplying.

statement.excerpt: That’s because, as I’ve said before, nobody can actually measure the ROI of AI, or even create a standard measurement of the cost of a task thanks to the inevitable hallucination-prone nature of LLMs and the ever-growing list of different harnesses and “agentic” (sigh) interfaces.

our_interpretation: The plain reading is a claim of measurement impossibility, not merely difficulty or uncertain future costs.
A standard task-cost measurement means a reproducible accounting method for defined tasks, models and execution procedures. It need not produce the same cost for every task.
A credible counterexample to either asserted impossibility contradicts the combined universal claim. Measuring task costs alone does not establish business ROI.
The causal claim is evaluated using work available before publication.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence establishes that neither deployment ROI nor reproducible costs for defined tasks can be measured because of model errors and changing execution systems.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A credible study measures deployment costs and attributable returns, or demonstrates reproducible cost accounting for defined AI tasks while recording unsuccessful attempts.

evidence.publisher: arXiv; Chunqiu Steven Xia and coauthors
evidence.explanation: The study defines average inference cost and token consumption alongside resolved-task rates, including unsuccessful problems in the benchmark. This supplies a reproducible task-cost measurement under the stated reading, without establishing complete business ROI.
This supports the narrower concern that agent evaluations often lack comparable, reproducible methods. It does not establish that constructing such measurements is impossible.
